server_tools.name: get_toolchanger_config
server_tools.summary: Toolchange and multi-extruder settings

server_tools.description: List the setting keys by category, with their descriptions on request: how to find the key for a setting (support_type, sparse_infill_density, wall_loops, ...).

category.description: per_object (default), print, filament, printer, toolchanger, project, or all

server_tools.name: get_valid_config_keys
server_tools.summary: Discover setting keys by category

server_tools.description: Install printer and filament presets the user has not installed, as the Setup Wizard does: a printer's vendor profiles are laid into the app's data folder when its vendor is not installed yet, and its model and nozzle are enabled; a filament is enabled. Names as get_presets {installed: false} lists them; a printer of a vendor whose folder does not begin its name (Bambu Lab's is BBL) needs vendor. Every preset is reloaded and the selected printer, print preset, filament slots and colours stay as they were (selection_kept) unless one is no longer shown for the printer (selection_changed names each), the filament maps put back (filament_maps_restored); a printer is not selected: next_steps names select_preset. Answers installed, already_installed, vendors_added, filaments_enabled (the filaments the app enables with a new printer too) and project_settings_changed. Refused while slicing, while a job runs, over unsaved preset changes (save_preset or reset_preset first) and while the project carries presets of its own (a 3MF's), which the reload would drop: save_project, new_project, install, then load_project the file again. Not undoable: it writes the data folder.

printers.description: Printer preset names, e.g. "Flashforge AD5X 0.4 nozzle"

vendor.description: The vendor of printers not installed, when its folder does not begin their names (e.g. "BBL")

server_tools.name: install_presets
server_tools.summary: Install printer or filament presets

server_tools.description: End the link the app keeps between the pieces of a cut, as the object list's Invalidate cut info does: until then a piece's solid parts and connectors cannot be moved or deleted on their own, and its pieces cannot be assembled. It ends it for every piece of that cut (objects lists them). An object that is not part of a cut changes nothing. One undo step.

object_id.description: Object index (0-based): any piece of the cut

server_tools.name: invalidate_cut_info
server_tools.summary: End a cut's link between its pieces

server_tools.description: List G-code files stored on the Flashforge printer.
server_tools.name: list_printer_files
server_tools.summary: G-code files stored on the printer

server_tools.description: Add a model file's objects (STL, 3MF, OBJ, STEP, ...) to the scene, keeping the current presets: a 3MF brings its geometry only, never its settings, and never renames the project. To open a 3MF as the project, with its settings, use load_project. next_steps names get_mesh_health for a loaded object with the mesh warning icon, and get_object_components for one with a part made of several shells (a loose part or stray fragment). loaded_objects carry get_scene_info's texture fields (texture_layers, needs_bake, model_uv): model_uv is true for an OBJ that brought its UVs.

multipart.description: When the file holds several objects at different heights, the slicer asks whether they are one object's parts. merge (default, as the GUI suggests) joins them into one object named after the file; separate keeps each as its own object. No other file is affected.

server_tools.name: load_model
server_tools.summary: Add a model's geometry; keeps presets

server_tools.description: Open a 3MF as the project: its objects, plates and presets replace the scene and the current settings, and unsaved project changes are discarded without asking. To add a model without changing the settings, use load_model. A running slice is cancelled first. Refused while the app's startup "restore unsaved items?" prompt waits (get_scene_info's open_dialogs), since it would orphan that backup.
server_tools.name: load_project
server_tools.summary: Open a 3MF project, replacing presets

server_tools.description: Match the project's filament slots to the printer's material station: for every loaded slot, pick a filament preset of the material the printer reports and set that slot's colour to the colour it reports. Slots the printer reports as empty are left untouched. Fixes the two things a stale project causes: send_to_printer refusing on a material mismatch, and a plate preview in the wrong colour. When the printer cannot be reached, the plan comes from its last known status (source: cached, with age_s and live_error) and changes the project only with allow_cached: true; a real run without it returns status not_applied with the plan and changes nothing.

allow_cached.description: Apply a plan made from the printer's last known status when it cannot be read live (default false). That status may be stale; age_s says how old it is.

dry_run.description: Report the plan without changing anything (default false). Each slot's 'changed' then means 'would change'.

slots.description: 1-based material-station slot ids to match. Omit for every loaded slot.

server_tools.name: match_project_to_printer
server_tools.summary: Match slots to the printer's filaments

server_tools.description: Merge an object's parts into one part, as the object list's Mesh boolean does: its solid parts are joined by a union and its negative volumes subtracted; its modifiers and support volumes, its parts' own settings and filaments, its layer ranges and brim ears are not carried (not_carried lists them); its name and object settings are. Every instance of the object becomes part of one mesh in one instance (instances_merged says so). When the union fails, the parts are joined without it (boolean says so). The merged object is the last object afterwards. Painting is cleared unless keep_painting keeps it. One undo step. An open toolbar tool is closed first (closed_toolbar_tool). Refused while an arrange, orient or bed fill runs.

keep_painting.description: Remap the painting (colour, supports, seams, fuzzy skin) onto the new meshes instead of clearing it; the app calls this experimental. Left out: the app's "Keep painted feature after mesh change" setting, which the answer's keep_painting_from names

server_tools.name: merge_parts
server_tools.summary: Merge an object's parts into one part

server_tools.description: Mirror an object across a plate axis, not the object's own: axis=z flips it top to bottom on the bed whatever its rotation. Mirroring is about the object's bounding-box centre, so it stays where it is, and a resting object stays on the bed (Z=0), as in the GUI. The response carries rotate_object's placement fields. With volume_id, that volume (a part or modifier) is mirrored about its own centre within the object, across the plate axis on instance 0.

axis.description: Plate axis to mirror across: x, y, or z

volume_id.description: Mirror this volume (as get_object_info lists them) within the object instead of the whole object

server_tools.name: mirror_object
server_tools.summary: Mirror an object across a plate axis

server_tools.description: Move object by offset (relative) or to position (relative=false). X/Y/Z are plate millimetres along the plate's own axes -- the same frame get_object_info and this tool's own "position" report, and independent of how the object is rotated. Moving an object into another plate's area re-homes it onto that plate, and the response carries rotate_object's placement fields. Every instance of the object moves by the same amount, so a multi-instance object keeps its arrangement. With volume_id, that volume (a part or modifier) moves within the object instead, in plate mm on instance 0, its box's centre as "position"; then, as the GUI does after a part moves, a floating object drops onto the bed (dropped_to_bed_mm). A one-volume object has no part to move on its own, and a cut object's solid parts wait for invalidate_cut_info.

volume_id.description: Move this volume (as get_object_info lists them) within the object instead of the whole object

x.description: Plate X in mm: a displacement along the plate's X axis when relative, else the X the bounding-box centre ends at

y.description: Plate Y in mm, same convention as x

z.description: Plate Z in mm (height above the bed), same convention as x

server_tools.name: move_object
server_tools.summary: Move an object, in plate mm

server_tools.description: Create a new empty project. Unsaved project changes are discarded without asking. A running slice is cancelled first. Refused while the app's startup "restore unsaved items?" prompt waits (get_scene_info's open_dialogs), since it would orphan that backup.
server_tools.name: new_project
server_tools.summary: Start a new, empty project

server_tools.description: Paint an object's surface as the GUI's paint tools do: filament colours for a multi-colour print, support enforcers and blockers, the seam, or fuzzy skin -- per-triangle data, the same the paint gizmos write. To put a whole object or volume on one filament, use set_object_filament. mode selects which: color (multi-material / MMU segmentation), support, seam, fuzzy_skin or texture. texture paints where one texture displacement layer applies (texture_layer: the layer's slot; state painted or none). selection selects where: bands along a plate axis (an even split across a list of filaments, or explicit ranges), a box, a sphere, the whole volume, or visible: the facets seen from `view` (front-facing and not hidden by the object's other facets), as the texture panel's Project only on visible does, in any mode; only the target instance's own model parts can hide a facet (other instances and objects never do), and view direction current is the 3D view's camera, the default one before the canvas has been drawn. connected fills the surface region around a seed without crossing an edge sharper than `angle` -- the way to paint a feature such as a bag or a sleeve; component paints one shell by id; state repaints every facet now in one state (match_filament, or match_state outside colour mode) with filament / state and leaves the rest, e.g. everything painted with filament 1 becomes filament 3 (remap_paint renumbers several at once). Very large meshes (millions of facets) take seconds to minutes; the work runs off the GUI thread, but the bridge's ORCAMCP_TIMEOUT (default 120 s) may still need raising. ALL COORDINATES ARE PLATE MILLIMETRES -- the same frame get_object_info reports its bounding_box and position in, not object-local coordinates. But for the numbers, use THIS call's own bounding_box in the response (or get_object_paint's), not get_object_info's: that one spans every instance of the object, and matches this tool's, which is instance_id's alone, only when the object has one instance. A facet belongs to the band or region containing its centroid. Paint lives on the volume, so it applies to every instance; instance_id only says whose transform reads your coordinates. Verify with get_object_paint, undo with undo, reset with clear_object_paint. Painted support enforcers do nothing while enable_support is off: next_steps then names the set_object_config call that turns it on with a (manual) support_type, for support only where painted. A paint panel open in the app is closed first, as the user would close it (closed_toolbar_tool), since it would write its own copy of the paint over this one. Texture paint changes the mask only: nothing reaches the print until the layers are baked into the mesh.

angle.description: selection=connected: stop at edges sharper than this many degrees (default 30, the gizmo's smart-fill default)

axis.description: Plate axis the bands run along (selection=bands)

bands.description: Explicit ranges in plate mm, each with a filament (mode=color) or a state. Ranges need not tile the object; facets outside them all are left alone.

component.description: selection=component: a shell id from get_object_components; needs volume_id when the object has several parts

filaments.description: One 1-based filament slot per band, split evenly along the axis (selection=bands, mode=color). 0 means unpainted.

from.description: Start of the even split in plate mm (default: the object's own extent). Ignored when explicit `bands` are given, which carry their own ranges.

instance_id.description: Which instance's transform reads your coordinates (default 0)

match_filament.description: selection=state, mode=color: repaint every facet now painted with this filament (0 = the unpainted facets)

match_state.description: selection=state, other modes: repaint every facet now in this state

replace.description: true (default) discards this mode's existing paint first; false paints on top of it. selection=state always keeps the rest: omit it there, or pass false

seed.description: selection=connected: {point: [x,y,z]} in plate mm (snapped to the surface), or {volume_id, facet} from pick_facet

state.description: State for selection=box/sphere/all/visible/connected/component/state when mode is not color. fuzzy_skin accepts none and enforcer (spelled either 'enforcer' or 'fuzzy_skin'), never blocker; texture accepts none and painted.

texture_layer.description: mode=texture (required there): the slot of the texture displacement layer whose paint this writes; the layer must exist. Not for other modes.

to.description: End of the even split in plate mm (default: the object's own extent). Ignored when explicit `bands` are given, which carry their own ranges.

view.description: selection=visible: the view the facets are seen from. Give direction or vector.

direction.description: A named view, or current: the 3D view's camera now

frame_layer.description: Only facets inside that texture layer's projection frame

vector.description: [x, y, z]: the direction the view looks along, in plate axes

volume_id.description: Part index within the object (0-based); omit, or pass -1, for every part

server_tools.name: paint_object
server_tools.summary: Paint color/support/seam/fuzzy/texture

server_tools.description: Find the facet a point, a ray, or a pixel of a render lands on. Give ONE of: point [x,y,z] (plate mm; snaps to the nearest surface), ray {origin, direction} (plate mm; first hit), or pixel [u,v] plus the `camera` object from a render_plate_view result (u right, v down, (0,0) top-left). Returns the volume, facet, plate point and normal -- feed `point` straight into paint_object {selection: "connected", seed: {point}}. include_component adds the shell id for paint_object {selection: "component"}; it costs a pass over the mesh. texture_layers lists the slots of the texture displacement layers whose paint covers part or all of the picked facet (empty when none).

camera.description: The `camera` object a render_plate_view view returned, unchanged

include_component.description: Also report the shell id of the hit facet (default false)

instance_id.description: Which instance's transform defines plate coordinates (default 0)

pixel.description: [u, v] in the render's pixels, (0,0) top-left; needs `camera`

point.description: Plate mm; the nearest surface point is picked

ray.description: Plate mm; the first surface along the ray is picked

volume_id.description: Restrict to one part (0-based); omit, or pass -1, to search every part

server_tools.name: pick_facet
server_tools.summary: The facet a point, ray or pixel hits

server_tools.description: Get an object's mesh ready for texture displacement, as the texture panel's Pro mode tools do. remesh rebuilds every model part with triangles near target_edge_mm (the painted area is carried onto the new triangles). subdivide with adaptive (default) refines the painted area only, to max_edge_mm and, with follow_texture, to the texture's detail within the budget_k; with adaptive false it splits every triangle of every part in four, steps times (more than 1 million triangles after the split is refused: the paint is remapped on the main thread), which drops the texture paint (texture_paint says so). smooth relaxes the baked vertices of the painted area with the stack's smoothing (strength, passes, ignore_outer_ring, stored when given); it runs on the app's main thread, so a part of more than 1 million triangles is refused, and an open panel is closed first. Runs in the call's wait (a little under the bridge's ORCAMCP_TIMEOUT): past it nothing changes. Answers each part's facets before and after. One undo step named as the panel names it; nothing to change is changed: false with the panel's words. Refused while a slice, an export, an arrange or orient, or the app's own bake or repair runs; an open toolbar tool is closed first, only when the call will change something.

adaptive.description: subdivide: refine the painted area only (default true); false splits every triangle of every part by steps

budget_k.description: adaptive subdivide: triangles to add, in thousands (default 750)

color_detail_mm.description: adaptive subdivide: triangle size where two colours meet, 0 off (default 0.3)

detail_mm.description: adaptive subdivide with follow_texture: how far the mesh may sit from the texture's shape (default 0.05)

edge_detail_mm.description: adaptive subdivide: triangle size along the painted area's outline, 0 off (default 0.4)

follow_texture.description: adaptive subdivide: spend triangles where the texture bends (default false)

ignore_outer_ring.description: smooth: hold the painted patch's rim out (default: the stack's)

keep_sharp_edges.description: remesh: hold hard edges in place (default true)

max_edge_mm.description: adaptive subdivide: no painted triangle stays larger (default: half the first part's mean edge)

min_edge_mm.description: adaptive subdivide with follow_texture: the smallest triangle (default 0.1)

operation.description: remesh: rebuild every model part with an even triangle size. subdivide: add triangles, adaptively where painted or uniformly. smooth: relax the painted area's baked vertices

sharp_angle_deg.description: remesh: how sharp a fold must be to be kept (default 40)

steps.description: subdivide with adaptive false: how many times every triangle is split in four (required then)

strength.description: smooth: percent a vertex moves toward its neighbours' average each pass (default: the stack's)

target_edge_mm.description: remesh: the triangle edge length (default: the first part's mean edge)

server_tools.name: prepare_texture_mesh
server_tools.summary: Remesh, subdivide or smooth for textures

server_tools.description: Start printing a G-code file already stored on the Flashforge printer, with optional material station mapping. Leveling and flow calibration each add minutes before the print; decide them as for send_to_printer. Omitted, each runs on a Creator 5 or 5 Pro when the file's estimated time, from the printer's file list, is 4 h or more, and not when the printer does not report one; other Flashforge models have not been checked, so there each stays off unless asked for. The response's print_options says what was sent and why. The tools are mapped by the file's own filaments, as the printer lists them (filaments_from: file), else the current project's (project). A file of several plates prints its first plate only, without asking (firmware 2.0.0). Refused while the printer runs a job or waits for its last one to be confirmed on its screen.

allow_material_mismatch.description: A mapped slot must hold the material family of the filament it feeds, or nothing is sent: the printer does not check, and prints the file's settings on whatever the slot holds (firmware 2.0.0 printed a PETG file on PLA at 255 C). true sends anyway.

auto_map.description: When true (default) and material_mappings is not given, build the mapping from the file's filament types (else the current project's) matched against the material station's loaded slots.

file_name.description: File name as returned by list_printer_files

flow_calibration.description: Calibrate the flow before printing. Omitted: on a Creator 5 or 5 Pro, on when the file's estimated time, from the printer's file list, is 4 h or more; off on other models.

leveling_before_print.description: Level the bed before printing. Omitted: on a Creator 5 or 5 Pro, on when the file's estimated time, from the printer's file list, is 4 h or more; off on other models.

material_mappings.description: Explicit tool-to-slot mapping. Overrides auto_map when provided.

color_delta_e.description: Accepted and ignored: the colour match a send reports per pair. Here so the material_mappings a response lists can be sent back as they are.

time_lapse.description: Ask the printer to record a time-lapse (default false). Not yet confirmed to take effect for a stored file.

server_tools.name: print_printer_file
server_tools.summary: Start printing a file on the printer

server_tools.description: Control the Flashforge printer as its Device page does: pause, resume or cancel the current job, turn the light on or off, set bed/chamber/nozzle target temperatures, switch the filtration fans (set_filtration: recirculation, exhaust), set the chamber and part-cooling fans (set_fans, 0-100 %), the print speed of the running job (set_print_speed: 50, 100, 125 or 166 %), or the Z offset (set_z_offset: mm, positive raises the nozzle, within -1 to 1 in 0.025 mm steps). It acts on the real printer. The set_* actions change only what they name: the printer's other settings are read first and sent back as it reports them; the answer gives what was sent and the printer's values before, and get_printer_status's printer.controls reads them back. Refused, sending nothing: a print speed while nothing prints, a fan or filtration the printer does not report, a status lacking a field the command sends back (it would go out as 0) or whose numbers no reading can be (telemetry_valid false), a value out of range, and an argument of another action.

bed.description: set_temperature only: target bed temperature, 0-150 C. Omit for no change.

chamber.description: set_temperature only: target chamber temperature, 0-100 C. Omit for no change.

chamber_fan.description: set_fans only: chamber fan speed, 0-100 %. Omit to leave it.

cooling_fan.description: set_fans only: part-cooling fan speed, 0-100 %. Omit to leave it.

cooling_left_fan.description: set_fans only: the left part-cooling fan, 0-100 %, on a printer that reports one.

exhaust.description: set_filtration only: the external (exhaust) filtration fan on or off. Omit to leave it.

nozzles.description: set_temperature only: per-tool target temperatures, 0-350 C. Tools not listed are left unchanged. set_temperature needs at least one of bed, chamber or a nozzle.

recirculation.description: set_filtration only: the internal (recirculation) filtration fan on or off. Omit to leave it.

speed.description: set_print_speed only: the running job's speed in percent, the printer's own steps.

z_offset.description: set_z_offset only: the Z offset in mm, positive raises the nozzle; -1 to 1 in 0.025 mm steps.

server_tools.name: printer_control
server_tools.summary: Job, light, temps, fans, speed, Z offset

server_tools.description: Quit OrcaMCP cleanly with no dialog. By default unsaved project changes are discarded, and a dialog the app is showing (get_scene_info's open_dialogs) is closed unanswered, with its own No or Cancel; the startup restore prompt keeps its backup for the next launch. Pass discard_changes=false to refuse while the project is dirty (call save_project first) or a dialog is open. A system file chooser or alert is never closed: quit_app refuses until the user closes it. If a dialog will not close within 10 s the app stays open with its changes kept, and active_warnings carries a QuitFailed entry saying why.

discard_changes.description: Discard unsaved project changes, and close open dialogs unanswered (default true)

server_tools.name: quit_app
server_tools.summary: Quit the app with no dialog

server_tools.description: Redo the last undone operation
server_tools.name: redo
server_tools.summary: Redo the last undone operation

server_tools.description: Reload an object's parts from the files they were loaded from, as the object list's Reload from disk does -- or, without object_id, every object, as the plate menu's Reload All does: each part takes its file's mesh as it is now, keeping its place, settings, filament and type (painting as the app's keep_painting setting says). volume_id reloads one part. A file is found where it was loaded from, else beside the object's own file; when it is in neither place the app asks for it, and file_path answers: a file of the same name there (its folder is then searched for the other missing ones), or another file, which replaces the part. Without file_path a missing file is refused, naming it. A piece of a cut is refused, as the object list's menu item is off for one; Reload All takes its parts loaded from a file, as the app's does (the parts the cut went through name no file). reloaded lists the parts loaded anew, with the placement; a file that fails to load is named in info_messages and the others are still reloaded. An open toolbar tool is closed first (closed_toolbar_tool). One undo step, taken only when something changed.

file_path.description: Where a source file that moved or was deleted is now, or another file to load into the part

object_id.description: The object to reload (default: every object)

volume_id.description: One part of object_id, as get_object_info numbers them

server_tools.name: reload_from_disk
server_tools.summary: Reload objects from their source files

server_tools.description: Renumber an object's painted filaments in one step: mapping {"1": 2, "2": 3, "3": 4} moves every facet painted with filament 1 to 2, 2 to 3 and 3 to 4 together -- never chained, so 1 does not end up at 3 -- which frees slot 1, e.g. for a support filament. Filaments the mapping does not list keep their facets. 0 means unpainted: as a key it paints the bare facets, as a value it unpaints. New filaments must be existing slots (get_filaments). One undo step. Returns facet counts per filament before and after (facets_before / facets_after, and per volume). Unpainted facets print with the part's own filament, which this leaves as it is: when the mapping moves that filament, notes names the set_object_filament call that moves them too. For one filament, paint_object with selection "state" does the same. mode texture renumbers one texture_layer's mask instead ({"0": 1, "1": 0} inverts it; clear_object_paint erases it); moving layers is set_texture_displacement, action move.

mapping.description: Old filament -> new filament, e.g. {"1": 2, "2": 3, "3": 4}, applied all at once

mode.description: Which paint to renumber: color, the filament paint (default), or texture, one texture layer's mask (texture_layer; its states are 0 unpainted and 1 painted). For support, seam or fuzzy skin states use paint_object's selection state.

texture_layer.description: mode=texture (required there): the slot of the layer whose mask is renumbered; the layer must exist

volume_id.description: Part index within the object (0-based); omit, or pass -1, for every part

server_tools.name: remap_paint
server_tools.summary: Renumber painted filaments in one step

server_tools.description: Rename an object, or with volume_id one of its volumes, as the object list's Rename does: the name of a one-part object's part follows the object's. Refused empty, or with a character the list refuses (<>:/\|?*"). changed: false for the name it already has: no undo step.

volume_id.description: Rename this volume (as get_object_info lists them) instead of the object

server_tools.name: rename_object
server_tools.summary: Rename an object or one of its parts

server_tools.description: Render a picture of a plate, one object, a region or a sliced layer's toolpaths (layer_view). Omit views for a contact sheet of iso, top and front fitted to the plate. A view is a preset (iso|top|front|back|left|right|low) or {camera_position, target} in BED mm (the get_scene_info frame; plate N sits at plates[N].bounding_box), or add frame: "plate_local" to give them relative to the plate's front-left corner. By default (camera_mode fit) a custom camera gives only the direction: the picture is zoomed to the view's fit -- the plate, {object_id}, a box {min, max} or a point with radius_mm -- and the eye may be moved back (camera.moved says so). camera_mode exact honours the eye, with fov_deg, or projection orthographic with ortho_height_mm. A close-up is a small fit box, not more pixels: camera.mm_per_pixel says the scale. Pass a camera a render returned as views[i].camera to draw exactly that view again. The requested plate's objects are drawn, including any hanging over its edge, from the 3D scene whichever tab the app shows. Every view returns objects_in_frame, uniform_image (+hint), plate_origin and the camera; overlays (outline, 10 mm grid, origin, labels) are on by default. paint draws support, seam, fuzzy_skin and texture-layer paint as the paint panels colour it (texture: one colour per layer, texture_layers to choose); colour paint is always drawn in its filaments' colours; texture_preview draws painted texture layers as the bake would make them, before baking; color_by filament draws every part in its filament's colour instead of one colour per object; color_by relief colours the depth of a texture's relief and color_by detail the facet angle of any mesh (pattern, aliasing, triangle-size bands). A view with compare_with draws the same camera as an earlier saved picture and sets it beside that picture and a mask of what changed (before/after a bake or an edit). section cuts the objects open with a plane and draws the cut faces, reporting their areas. Use save_to_file=true for PNG paths. layer_view draws a top-down plan instead: "first_layer", or any sliced layer as {layer: N} or {z: mm}, filtered by features and filaments, with the layer's height, filaments and extruded areas -- the way to check supports, interfaces and which tool prints what on a given layer.

color_by.description: object (default): one colour per object, so objects tell apart. filament: each part in its filament's colour, as the 3D view. With paint, unpainted surfaces are neutral grey, so object and filament only matter without it. objects_in_frame[].color_source says where each part's colour came from: palette, filament, paint (colour paint, always its filaments' colours), neutral (paint tints asked for), relief or detail. relief: colour each facet by how far it lies above (red) or below (blue) the surface the part had before its texture, white at it: with texture_preview the unbaked surface is the reference (what the texture adds); after a bake_texture_displacement of this session the mesh the bake displaced is (kept in memory until the project is closed, 8 parts, and used only while the part still has the baked mesh -- an undo, repair or new bake drops it); for any other part (a mesh baked in the texture panel, a model loaded already textured, an earlier session's bake) there is no reference and the part keeps its colour, listed in relief.not_coloured with the reason. The distance is to the nearest point of the reference surface, not along the displacement, so steep relief reads shallower. Values are in bed mm, the instance's scale included. The scale spans the 99th percentile of |distance| (range_source measured_p99; the true extremes are in min_mm and max_mm, the facets beyond it in beyond_scale); a second bake of a part measures that bake's own increment. The answer's relief gives the scale (from, to, bins, step in mm, range_source), a legend of each colour step's range, per object and part the reference, min_mm, max_mm and mean_abs_mm, and notes; the colours are shaded by the lights, so read the legend by hue and rake the light for relief. detail: needs no reference and works on any mesh: each facet is coloured by its largest angle to the facets it shares an edge with (pale = flat or smooth, dark = sharp), which shows a texture's pattern, the stair-stepping of one sampled too coarsely and bands where the mesh's triangles change size (but a band of large flat triangles is pale, its angles being 0: use triangle_size for density); the answer's detail gives the scale in degrees, per part the angle statistics, open_edges, edge_mm (triangle edge length min, median, max in mm) and slabs. triangle_size: each facet coloured by its longest edge in mm on a log scale (blue fine, red coarse), which shows aliasing bands and changes of density that facet angles cannot; the answer's triangle_size gives the legend in mm and per part longest_edge_mm statistics, beyond_scale and slabs: the median longest edge per 2 mm slab of bed Z (at most 64 slabs), so a band shows in numbers. With texture_preview these three colour the unbudgeted preview, which cannot predict the bands the bake's own triangle budget makes: bake, then colour the baked mesh. A degenerate facet is skipped as a neighbour. With texture_preview all colour the displaced preview; colour-painted parts coloured this way lose their filament colours. A part over 1 million triangles is not coloured (too_large), one picture colours at most 2 million triangles, and the work must finish within the call's wait. 3D views only.

detail_range_deg.description: With color_by detail: the facet angle in degrees that takes the darkest colour (12 steps from 0). Default: the measured 98th percentile, rounded up to a whole degree.

image_format.description: png or jpeg. Default: png when save_to_file is true (crisp overlays, alpha kept), jpeg for inline base64 (smaller).

layer_view.description: Instead of a 3D render, a top-down plan; ignores views. "first_layer": the first layer -- object footprints (or their raft), brim loops, support and wipe tower -- from the sliced plate (source: sliced) or the model footprints when unsliced (source: footprints); the view for 'is the brim wide enough' and 'where do the support feet land'. {layer: N} or {z: mm}: any layer of the sliced G-code, the lines the Preview draws (source: gcode; an unsliced plate is an error). Returns layer {number, of, z}, filaments (printing on it, in order), extruded_mm2 by feature and extruded_mm2_by_filament (line length x width, the whole layer whatever is drawn), object_mm2 vs support_mm2, objects_at_height (per object its object_layer and support_layer printed at this height -- support can have heights of its own, so either can be null -- and overhang: area_mm2 hanging past the layer below and support_below, the first support layer going down, at most 2 mm, whose lines lie under this overhang -- z, gap_mm down to it, and the support_mm2 and interface_mm2 of the overhang they lie under; a gap near the configured top Z distance means that is the contact layer. When none within 2 mm has lines under it, support_below is the nearest support layer below with 0 areas and searched_to_mm 2: nothing touches the overhang. null means no support layer below at all), drawn, legend, and nothing_drawn (+hint) when the filter matches no line.

color_by.description: feature (default): the Preview's feature colours. filament: each slot's colour, as the Preview's Filament view. The legend says which colour is which.

filaments.description: Draw only these filament slots, 1-based as get_scene_info's filaments_used (default all).

fit.description: "plate" (default) or {"object_id": n} to frame that object (object_index is the same number, kept) with what it prints on this layer: its support lines, and on the first layer its brim and raft.

layer.description: Layer number from 1, as the Preview's layer slider numbers layers: 1..get_print_estimate's printed_layers.

z.description: A height in mm; the nearest printed layer is drawn (a tie goes to the lower).

light.description: "default" (the 3D view's two lights) or a single directional light that rakes across a surface so relief reads. To rake what a view shows, use {from: "left"|"right"|"top"|"bottom", elevation_deg}: the light comes from that side of each view's image, elevation_deg (1 to 90, default 20) above the surface the camera sees, so low grazes it and shows relief; {from: "front"} lights from the camera. It turns with each view's camera. In bed axes instead: {azimuth_deg, elevation_deg} (azimuth 0 = from +X, counter-clockwise seen from above, elevation 1 to 90 above the horizon) or {direction: [x, y, z]}, the way the light travels (from the light to the scene); these can light a face from behind, giving a dark picture. A face square to the light is drawn at about 0.9 of its colour, one turned away at about 0.28; no highlight. The answer's light gives the bed-axes direction used (direction, azimuth_deg, elevation_deg; bed_elevation_deg with from) and applied: false with a warning when the render shader could not be used (shader_fallback) or nothing was drawn. 3D views only.

applied.description: Accepted back from an answer; ignored

azimuth_deg.description: Bed axes. Degrees; 0 = light from +X, counter-clockwise seen from above

bed_elevation_deg.description: Accepted back from an answer; ignored

direction.description: [x, y, z] the way the light travels, bed axes

elevation_deg.description: Degrees, 1 to 90: above the horizon (bed axes) or above the surface the camera sees (from)

from.description: Camera-relative: the side of the image the light comes from

warning.description: Accepted back from an answer; ignored

overlays.description: Self-locating overlays drawn on the image: plate outline, 10 mm grid, origin with X/Y, numbered object labels, hatched excluded areas and collision volumes (a height-limited one drawn at its height; in a layer plan, dashed when not at that layer). true/omitted = all, false = none, or an object {outline, grid, origin, labels, excluded} of booleans.

paint.description: Paint to tint on the parts, as the paint panels colour it: support and seam enforcers light green and blockers light red, fuzzy_skin light green, texture one colour per layer (texture_layers chooses). The unpainted surface is then drawn neutral grey so the tints read. Colour paint is always drawn in its filaments' colours, without this. The answer's tint_legend gives each tint's colour and, per object, its facets (get_object_paint's count) and area_mm2 (one instance). A texture mask its mesh has outgrown is not drawn and is marked stale; tint_notes explains an empty case. Ask one channel at a time to tell support from seam in the picture: they share the panels' colours. 3D views only.

relief_range_mm.description: With color_by relief: the colour scale's half range in mm (the colours run from minus this to plus this, 15 steps); facets beyond it take the end colours (counted in beyond_scale). Default: the 99th percentile of the measured |distance|, so a few spikes do not wash the rest out.

save_to_file.description: Return file paths instead of base64 (default: false)

section.description: Cut the objects open with a plane and draw the cut faces dark grey, as the 3D view's section view does; the side the normal points to is removed. "app": the cut the 3D view shows now (an error when its section view is off). {normal, point}: the plane through point with that normal. {normal, ratio}: the section view's own sweep, ratio above 0 to 1, from the end of the bounding sphere of the plate's instances the normal points to (0, nothing cut) to the opposite end (1, everything). {plane: x|y|z, at_mm}: square to an axis, removing the larger coordinates (remove: below removes the smaller). Points and at_mm are bed mm, or plate-local with frame: plate_local. The answer's section gives the plane used (normal, point) and per object section_area_mm2, islands and effect (cut, keeps_all or removes_all); empty with a note when the plane cuts no object, and a note for an object with open edges, whose cut face may be short (slicing drops an open outline). The cut is limited to z >= 0 (a sunk part's cut below the bed is neither drawn nor counted). It needs the render shader (an error when this driver could not build it), works with any camera and light, and paint tints are cut with the surface. 3D views only.

applied.description: Accepted back from an answer; ignored

at_mm.description: With plane: where it cuts along that axis

cap_color.description: Accepted back from an answer; ignored

empty.description: Accepted back from an answer; ignored

frame.description: Frame of point and of at_mm for x and y (default bed_mm)

normal.description: Unit or not: the side it points to is removed

notes.description: Accepted back from an answer; ignored

objects.description: Accepted back from an answer; ignored

plane.description: The axis the plane is square to

ratio.description: With normal: the 3D view's ratio, 0 (nothing cut) to 1 (everything)

ratio_used.description: Accepted back from an answer; ignored

remove.description: With plane: above (default) removes the larger coordinates

removes.description: Accepted back from an answer; ignored

source.description: Accepted back from an answer; ignored

warning.description: Accepted back from an answer; ignored

texture_layers.description: With paint texture: only these layer slots (0 to 7). Default: every slot a texture stack on the plate has a layer in. A slot nothing is painted in is listed with no objects.

texture_preview.description: Draw each textured object as its bake would make it -- the true displaced surface and the texture's colours, with the part's own colour paint kept, computed as the bake computes it (a classic part: after its preparation) but without simplification, as the texture panel's preview -- instead of the flat unbaked mesh. Nothing is baked or changed. It takes time on large meshes: when every view fits an object (fit {object_id}, or a box or point that only some reach) only those objects are previewed, otherwise all of them. The answer's texture_preview says which objects were drawn, how long each took, whether it was kept from an earlier call (cached: the last 4 objects or 2 million triangles are kept until the object's layers, paint, mesh or palette change), and which were left out and why. An object whose preview does not finish within the call's wait is drawn unbaked and listed timed_out (not_reached when the wait ran out before it was started); a part over 1 million triangles is too_large. Not with paint texture, a section or a layer_view. Default false.

views.description: Views to render. Omit for the default contact sheet (iso, top, front). Each view: a preset with optional fit, or camera_position + target (bed mm unless frame is plate_local).

camera.description: A camera object an earlier render returned (views[i].camera), unchanged, to draw exactly that view again at its resolution. Takes no other key in the view, except compare_with.

camera_mode.description: fit (default): camera_position and target give the direction, the picture is zoomed to `fit` and the eye may be moved back. exact: the eye is at camera_position, looking at target, with fov_deg (perspective) or ortho_height_mm (orthographic); takes no preset or fit.

camera_position.description: [x, y, z] in bed mm, same frame as get_scene_info

compare_with.description: The file_path of an earlier render_plate_view picture of this session (a PNG, saved with save_to_file, of this plate): the view is drawn with that picture's camera and size, and the answer's picture is three columns of that size -- before, now, and the difference (now in grey, the pixels whose colour changed by more than 24 of 255 in red). comparison gives changed_fraction, changed_box [x0, y0, x1, y1] in a column's pixels, and the columns' x_offsets; the picture is one for the eye and these numbers, not one to compare with later. Send the same overlays, light, section and paint in both pictures, or those differences count as changes. Takes no preset, fit or camera of its own (only the earlier picture's own camera, unchanged), one view per call, and not with layer_view. A path that is not one of this server's pictures, one not rendered in this session, a JPEG, another plate or another resolution is refused. Nothing is undone or changed to make the earlier state: to see a change, render before it with save_to_file, make it, then render with compare_with.

fit.description: "plate" (default), {"object_id": n} to frame one object -- its instances on this plate; an object this plate does not hold is an error naming its plate (object_index is the same number, kept) --, {box: {min: [x,y,z], max: [x,y,z]}} to frame a region, or {point: [x,y,z], radius_mm: r} to frame a sphere; coordinates in bed mm, or plate-local with the view's frame. A close-up is a small fit, not more pixels.

box.description: A region to frame: its corners in mm.

point.description: [x, y, z] centre of the sphere to frame (with radius_mm)

radius_mm.description: Radius in mm of the sphere around point (above 0)

fov_deg.description: camera_mode exact, perspective: the vertical field of view in degrees, 5 to 120 (default 30).

frame.description: Frame of camera_position/target and of a fit box or point: bed_mm (default, the get_scene_info frame) or plate_local (from this plate's front-left corner).

ortho_height_mm.description: camera_mode exact, orthographic: the height of the image in mm (required there, above 0).

plate_index.description: See view_matrix: the plate the camera was drawn of; a replay on another plate is refused.

preset.description: Named camera framing `fit` (default the plate). low = bed level from the front, for first layers and support feet.

target.description: [x, y, z] in bed mm; point it at the plate's objects (get_scene_info positions)

view_matrix.description: A returned camera, sent as the view itself (view_matrix, projection_matrix, viewport and the keys below it carries): drawn exactly, like camera. The keys type, pixel_origin, mm_per_pixel, moved, requested_position, replayed and input_frame are accepted and ignored; camera_mode, projection, fov_deg, camera_position, target, preset and fit are ignored there too.

viewport.description: See view_matrix: [x, y, width, height], a square.

server_tools.name: render_plate_view
server_tools.summary: Render a plate, object or sliced layer

server_tools.description: Repair an object's mesh with the app's own repair -- the object list's Repair (Fix Model), on every platform: each volume is repaired in place, its cracks welded, its shells oriented consistently, its holes (open edges, non-manifold) filled, its self-intersections removed and its shells of fewer than 4 facets removed. No volume is split or deleted; a closed stray shell stays in its volume (get_object_components lists shells). A volume from which no solid can be built (flat or empty) is left as it is, and the answer says so. The object is then dropped onto the bed. A repaired volume's painting is cleared unless keep_painting keeps it. One undo step. When there is a repair to apply, an open toolbar tool (gizmo) is closed first, as the Repair needs, and the answer names it (closed_toolbar_tool); closing a painting tool records its own undo step, as when the user closes it. Nothing changes when there is nothing to repair, when the call is refused or fails, or when the repair takes longer than this call may wait (a little under the bridge's ORCAMCP_TIMEOUT). The answer: get_mesh_health's numbers before and after, `repair` (volumes repaired, vertices welded, triangles removed, shells reversed, holes filled, shells removed, self-intersections removed), whether painting was kept, and the object's placement. Refused while a slice, an export or an upload runs (wait_for_slice first), or an arrange or orient. A large mesh can take minutes. Give exactly one of object_id (one object; volume_id for one of its volumes), plate_index (every object with an instance on that plate, as the plate's Fix All) or all_plates: true (every object in the project, as Fix All Plates; locked plates are not skipped, as the app does not skip them). For several objects: they are repaired one after another within this call's one wait; those finished in time are applied together in one undo step, and the rest are left as they are. The answer's `objects` gives each one's result -- repaired, nothing_to_repair, failed (some volume no solid can be built from; the others are still repaired), changed_meanwhile (changed in the app during the repair: left as it is), deleted_meanwhile (deleted in the app during it) or timed_out (not reached within the wait, or not applied within 10 s past it; next_steps names repair_mesh for it) -- `counts` as the app counts them, and `repair` summed.

all_plates.description: true: repair every object in the project -- on every plate, locked ones included, and on none -- as Fix All Plates does. Instead of object_id

keep_painting.description: Remap the object's painting (colour, supports, seams, fuzzy skin) onto the repaired mesh instead of clearing it; the app calls this experimental. Left out: the app's "Keep painted feature after mesh change" setting, which the answer's keep_painting_from names

object_id.description: Object index (0-based): repair this one object. Give object_id, plate_index or all_plates

plate_index.description: Repair every object with an instance on this plate (0-based, get_scene_info's plate_index), as the plate's Fix All does. Instead of object_id; the current plate stays as it is

volume_id.description: Repair only this volume (0-based, as get_mesh_health's volumes list them), as the object list's Repair does for a selected part. Left out: every volume. Only with object_id

server_tools.name: repair_mesh
server_tools.summary: Repair a mesh: close holes, open edges

server_tools.description: Replace a part's mesh with another 3D file (STL, 3MF, STEP, OBJ, ...), as the object list's Replace 3D file does: the new mesh takes the part's place, settings, filament, type and name (the object's too when it has one part), and painting as the app's keep_painting setting says. The file must hold one part. volume_id names the part (needed when the object has several). folder instead replaces every part of the object (or volume_id's) with the file of its source file's name in that folder, as Replace all with 3D files does, skipping parts whose file is not there. A piece of a cut is refused. An open toolbar tool is closed first (closed_toolbar_tool). replaced lists the parts loaded anew, with the placement. One undo step per part replaced, as the app takes (none when nothing was).

file_path.description: The new file for the part

folder.description: Or a folder holding a file of each part's source file name

volume_id.description: The part, as get_object_info numbers them (needed with several)

server_tools.name: replace_volume_with_file
server_tools.summary: Replace a part's mesh with another file

server_tools.description: Remove per-object setting overrides, or with volume_id those of one part or modifier.

keys.description: Keys to reset. If omitted, resets every override but the object's filament (extruder), which stays, as the GUI's reset leaves it. An empty list is refused. reset_count says how many were cleared; a reset that clears nothing changes nothing.

volume_id.description: Reset this volume's overrides (as get_object_info lists them) instead of the object's; its filament (extruder) stays, as the part's reset in the app leaves it

server_tools.name: reset_object_config
server_tools.summary: Remove an object's or part's overrides

server_tools.description: Discard unsaved preset changes.
server_tools.name: reset_preset
server_tools.summary: Discard unsaved preset edits

server_tools.description: Rotate object around the plate's X, Y and Z axes (degrees), not the object's own axes: a z=90 turns the object about the vertical whatever its current rotation is. Applied in the order X, then Y, then Z, about the object's bounding-box centre so it turns in place, then, as the GUI does, dropped back onto the bed (Z=0) unless it was sinking below it before. The resulting rotation_degrees are the instance's, the same numbers get_object_info reports. The response reports, for afterwards, the placement fields: instance_placement (each instance's plate and whether it is inside it), plate_index (instance 0's plate), plate_indices and on_bed (every instance inside its own plate). With volume_id, that volume (a part or modifier) turns about its own centre within the object, in the plate's axes on instance 0, and the object is dropped as the GUI drops it (dropped_to_bed_mm).

relative.description: true (the default): x, y and z are the change in degrees. false is refused: absolute rotation is not supported, so work out the change from rotation_degrees in get_object_info.

volume_id.description: Rotate this volume (as get_object_info lists them) within the object instead of the whole object

x.description: Rotation about the plate's X axis (degrees)

y.description: Rotation about the plate's Y axis (degrees)

z.description: Rotation about the plate's Z axis, the vertical (degrees)

server_tools.summary: Rotate an object about plate axes

server_tools.description: Save the edited settings of the print, filament or printer preset, to that preset or with name as a new one, as the settings tab's Save does. A filament preset saved under a new name takes over every slot that used the old one (the answer's slots), and one saved from a system preset is made compatible with the selected printer only. A system preset cannot be overwritten: give a name.

name.description: Save as new name. If omitted, saves to current preset.

server_tools.name: save_preset
server_tools.summary: Save edited settings to a preset

server_tools.description: Save the current project. Without output_path it overwrites the file the project is named after (the last load_project, export_3mf or save_project path); pass output_path to name it, or to save under a new name.

output_path.description: Path of the .3mf to save to. Required while the project has no file name; naming it any other way needs a file dialog, which MCP cannot open. Also acts as Save As.

server_tools.name: save_project
server_tools.summary: Save the project, in place or as a copy

server_tools.description: Scale object along the plate's X, Y and Z axes, not the object's own: with uniform=false, z is the object's height above the bed whatever its rotation. uniform=true uses x for all axes and is frame-independent. Scaling is about the object's bounding-box centre, so it grows in place, and then, as the GUI does, the object is dropped back onto the bed (Z=0) unless it was sinking below it before. Factors must be positive; use mirror_object to flip an axis. A non-uniform scale along plate axes on an object whose rotation is not a multiple of 90 degrees is a shear -- it is applied, and the response says so in skew_warning. The response carries rotate_object's placement fields. With volume_id, that volume (a part or modifier) scales about its own centre within the object, along the plate's axes on instance 0, and the object is dropped as the GUI drops it (dropped_to_bed_mm).

uniform.description: If true, x scales every axis, so give x (default: false)

volume_id.description: Scale this volume (as get_object_info lists them) within the object instead of the whole object

x.description: Scale factor along the plate's X axis (must be > 0)

y.description: Scale factor along the plate's Y axis (must be > 0)

z.description: Scale factor along the plate's Z axis, the vertical (> 0)

server_tools.name: scale_object
server_tools.summary: Scale an object along plate axes

server_tools.description: Select a plate as current. Refused while an arrange, orient or bed fill runs: a plate's arrange applies its result to the current plate.

server_tools.summary: Make a plate the current one

server_tools.description: Select a printer, filament, or print preset by name. With type 'filament', pass slot (1-based) to set just that filament slot, like the sidebar filament combo; without slot, only with one physical slot (since 2.5.0.6: with several it is refused, as it changed no slot), and dirty preset changes are discarded. With type 'printer', the response lists the resulting filaments (slot, preset, colour, previous_color) and, per slot, color_source as observed across the switch: 'unchanged', 'remembered' (the colour last saved for that printer, applied by Remember printer configuration, on by default), 'default' (#26A69A for a slot nothing was saved for) or 'other'. colors_source sums them up, 'mixed' when they differ. To change individual settings, use apply_config.

slot.description: Filament slot to set, 1-based. Only valid with type 'filament'.

server_tools.name: select_preset
server_tools.summary: Switch a preset, or one filament slot's

server_tools.description: Select a printer: a Bambu device by dev_id, or a printer preset with a print host by name. A switch of printer preset also reports the resulting filaments and colors_source, as select_preset {type: printer} does.

physical_printer.description: Printer preset with a print host, as listed by get_printers

server_tools.name: select_printer
server_tools.summary: Select a Bambu device or a print host

server_tools.description: Upload the sliced plate to the configured print host and START PRINTING IT: start_print defaults to true, so a bare call begins a print on real hardware. Pass start_print=false to upload only. The upload runs without any dialog: on a Flashforge printer with a material station the project's filaments are mapped onto the loaded slots automatically (pass material_mappings to choose the slots yourself). Pass direct=false to open OrcaSlicer's send dialog and leave the send to the user. Refused, as the GUI's Print and Send buttons are off, when a plate it would send failed the check its slice ran on its G-code (get_slicing_status's plates[].gcode_check). On a Flashforge the printer can calibrate the flow and level the bed before it starts; each adds minutes, and the choice is yours: pass flow_calibration and leveling_before_print true before a long print or after a filament, nozzle or bed change, false for a short print or a repeat soon after the last one on the same filaments (get_printer_status's last_print_started_here says when this OrcaMCP instance last started a print there, and with what). Omitted, each runs on a Creator 5 or 5 Pro when the plate's estimated time is 4 h or more; other Flashforge models have not been checked, so there each stays off unless asked for. time_lapse is off unless asked for. The response's print_options says what was sent and why. An explicit true is refused where it would be ignored: direct=false, start_print=false (nothing starts; pass them to print_printer_file then), another print host, or a Flashforge without its serial number and check code; so are use_material_station: true and a material_mappings list, except with start_print=false, where the upload carries them. With start_print=false every print option is sent off.

all_plates.description: Dialog sends only (direct=false): send all plates instead of the current one.

allow_material_mismatch.description: A mapped slot must hold the material family of the filament it feeds, or nothing is sent: the printer does not check, and prints the file's settings on whatever the slot holds (firmware 2.0.0 printed a PETG file on PLA at 255 C). true sends anyway. Direct sends to a Flashforge host with local-API credentials only; true is refused anywhere else.

direct.description: When true (default), upload straight to the printer. When false, open OrcaSlicer's send dialog for the user instead.

file_name.description: Name to store the upload under (default: the plate's own output file name). Direct sends only.

flow_calibration.description: Calibrate the flow before printing. Omitted: on a Creator 5 or 5 Pro, on when the plate's estimated time is 4 h or more; off on other models. Direct sends that start the print on a Flashforge host with local-API credentials only; true is refused anywhere else.

leveling_before_print.description: Level the bed before printing. Omitted: on a Creator 5 or 5 Pro, on when the plate's estimated time is 4 h or more; off on other models. Direct sends that start the print on a Flashforge host with local-API credentials only; true is refused anywhere else.

material_mappings.description: Explicit tool-to-slot mapping. Omit to map the project's filaments onto matching loaded slots automatically. Direct sends to a Flashforge host with local-API credentials only; a mapping is refused anywhere else.

color_delta_e.description: Accepted and ignored: the colour match a send reports per pair. Here so the material_mappings a response lists can be sent back as they are.

start_print.description: Start printing once the upload finishes (default true). Direct sends only.

time_lapse.description: Ask the printer to record a time-lapse (default false). Direct sends that start the print on a Flashforge host with local-API credentials only; true is refused anywhere else.

use_material_station.description: Print from the material station (default: true when the printer reports one). Direct sends to a Flashforge host with local-API credentials only; true is refused anywhere else.

server_tools.name: send_to_printer
server_tools.summary: Upload the plate AND START printing it

server_tools.description: Place brim ears on an object -- the small tabs the brim adds at chosen points. Brim ears are NOT facet paint: they are points on the object (ModelObject::brim_points), so they have their own tool. Positions are PLATE millimetres, the same frame get_object_info reports its bounding_box in -- but for the numbers, use THIS call's own bounding_box in the response (or get_object_paint's), not get_object_info's: that one spans every instance of the object, and matches this tool's, instance 0's, only when the object has one instance. Only x and y matter, because an ear always sits on the bottom of the object. Brim ears are stored per object, not per instance, and slicing resolves them through instance 0 only, so instance_id must be 0 (or omitted), and this response's bounding_box is always instance 0's regardless. Pass an empty points array with append left false to remove them all. They only produce brim unless brim_type is 'painted'.

append.description: false (default) replaces the object's ears; true adds to them

instance_id.description: Must be 0 (or omitted): brim ears are object-level data and slicing resolves them through instance 0 only

points.description: Ear positions in plate mm. An empty array removes every ear, when append is left false.

z.description: Accepted and ignored: an ear always sits on the object's underside. Here so the brim_ears a response lists can be sent back as they are.

radius.description: Default radius for points that do not carry one (default 5.0 mm)

Read the response, not just status: effective_filaments is every slot the object still prints with (volumes, painted facets, layer ranges); cleared_overrides lists each volume that lost its own slot and what it held; other_slots lists slots its volumes still force. The object is on one filament only when effective_filaments has one entry. get_object_info's `volumes` shows the same per volume; get_scene_info's filaments_used shows it per object. changed: false when the call set what was already there: no undo step, and the plates keep their slice. server_tools.description: Set settings for a Z height range. z_min/z_max are measured from the object's own base, not from the bed, so they equal plate Z only while the object sits on the bed -- moving the object up does not move its ranges. A range always has a layer_height and an extruder, as the GUI's object list gives it: the object's own (its layer_height, else the process preset's, within what the nozzle of the extruder printing the range prints; extruder 0, the object's) unless settings give one. The range as stored must print on that nozzle: a layer_height outside the printer's min_layer_height..max_layer_height for the extruder that prints the range (its own, else the object's) is rejected, and so is an extruder whose nozzle cannot print the range's height (rejected_values). A call that applies nothing, or gives no settings, is an error and leaves the ranges as they were.

Only what the call gives changes, in one undo step; the answer's settings are in this tool's argument shape (sent back, they change nothing), effective says what applies. "global" follows the printer's and print settings. A plate whose slicing settings change is made the current plate first, as the dialog does. spiral_vase "on" is the dialog's Enable answered Yes: every object on the plate gets the vase's object settings (one wall, no top shell, no infill, no support), which are the object's, so its copies on other plates print with them too (vase_settings_applied lists them); "off" and "global" leave those settings on the objects. A plate's own bed_type is offered for Bambu Lab printers only (elsewhere the plate follows the global one, apply_config's project curr_bed_type). The same settings again: changed false, no undo step; a value the plate already has is never refused. Refused while an arrange, orient or bed fill runs (an arrange of every plate locks and unlocks plates as it runs).

print_sequence.description: Print the plate by layer or by object

spiral_vase.description: "on" also gives every object on the plate the vase's object settings (see the description); "global" follows the print settings

server_tools.description: Add, edit, move or remove one texture displacement layer of an object, as the texture displacement panel does. An object holds up to 8 layers, combined in slot order; each applies where paint_object (mode texture) paints it, and nothing reaches the print until the layers are baked into the mesh. add takes the first free slot with texture (an id from get_texture_library) or the library's first; file_path imports an image (an identical one already in the library is reused, imported_texture says which); edit changes only what is given; move puts a layer at to_position in slot order, its paint with it (it may take another slot: layer in the answer); remove drops it and its paint. projection view projects from view_direction (a named view, or current: the 3D view's camera now) or view_axes; projection_frame projects once through a rectangle (view or right and up, center, width_mm, height_mm) with tiling off, as the panel's Apply does it also paints the layer where the frame sees the surface (facets_painted); false clears it; adjust_image saves an adjusted copy of the texture into the library and uses it. One undo step; nothing to change is changed: false. Refused while an arrange, orient or bake runs; an open toolbar tool is closed first when the call changes something.

action.description: add: a new layer in the first free slot; edit: change the layer in slot layer; remove: drop it and its paint; move: put it at to_position

adjust_image.description: Save an adjusted copy of the layer's image into the library and use it

blend.description: How the layer combines with the layers below it (the base layer ignores it)

color.description: Colour the painted area from the texture's own colours (a colour texture only)

color_mix.description: Stack-wide: interleave filament pairs to reach colours between them

color_mix_count.description: Stack-wide: the most mixed colors the palette may offer

depth_mm.description: Maximum displacement along the surface normal, in mm

edge_fade.description: Fade the displacement toward the edge of the painted patch

edge_fade_amount.description: How far edge_fade reaches into the painted patch

file_path.description: An image file (png, jpg, bmp) to use as the texture: imported into the texture library, or the identical texture already there reused. Instead of texture

layer.description: The layer's slot (edit, remove, move). add takes the first free slot

midlevel.description: The height that does not move the surface: 0 only raises, 0.5 lets dark texels cut in

object_id.description: Object index (0-based). The layers belong to the object

projection.description: How the texture is mapped: triplanar, cylindrical, spherical, unwrap, view (from a view), model_uv (the model's own UV channel)

projection_frame.description: Project the texture once through a rectangle (view or right and up, center, width_mm, height_mm) with tiling off; false clears the frame

tile_size_mm.description: Size of one texture tile, in mm

to_position.description: move: the 0-based position in slot order

view_axes.description: projection view: the projector's right and up axes in plate axes, as a layer reports them

right.description: The projector's right axis in plate axes

up.description: The projector's up axis in plate axes

server_tools.description: Edit the unwrap of a texture displacement layer whose projection is unwrap, as the texture panel's UV pane does, in its order: seam_angle_deg and auto_connect_islands, seams (add_seams, remove_seams, clear_seams, seam_paths snapped to the nearest vertices, cut_islands), then the unwrap is made anew when seams or the angle changed (its charts are numbered anew, and the islands are laid out as a net when the layer asks for it), relayout, islands (placement by chart), join, unjoin, average_scale, clear_uv_edits, uv_edits. Chart and vertex numbers name the unwrap as get_texture_unwrap reports it before this call (pass its unwrap_id to have a stale number refused), so a call that changes seams or the angle takes no island or vertex edit: send those in a second call. Refused: an unknown chart or vertex, a join of charts that share no edge, a seam that is no mesh edge, a layer that is not an unwrap or is painted nowhere on the owner part. One undo step named as the panel names the edit, none for no change (changed false); an open toolbar tool is closed first when the call changes something. Answers the unwrap as get_texture_unwrap does.

add_seams.description: Mesh edges to cut along, as [vertex, vertex] pairs of the owner part's mesh

auto_connect_islands.description: Lay islands out as a connected net; turning it on lays them out now

average_scale.description: Give every island the mean of the islands' scales

cut_islands.description: Charts to cut in two across their longest axis (a seam is added)

islands.description: Place islands by chart; only the fields given change. An entry of get_texture_unwrap's islands is accepted as it is

offset.description: Where the island sits, in the unwrap's mm

rotation_deg.description: Rotation about the island's own centre, in degrees

scale.description: Size factor about the island's own centre (1: the size the unwrap gave it)

join.description: Unfold a chart against a neighbour it shares an edge with and group the two, so they are one island

to.description: The neighbour to join to (default: the nearest one)

layer.description: The slot of an unwrap layer that is painted on the object's first model part

relayout.description: Lay the islands out as a connected net again

remove_seams.description: Seams to take away, as [vertex, vertex] pairs

seam_angle_deg.description: Edges sharper than this cut the unwrap into islands (the panel's Seam angle); once the layer has any seam, only seams cut

seam_paths.description: Seams along the shortest path over mesh edges between two points

from.description: Plate mm; snapped to the nearest vertex of the owner part

to.description: Plate mm; snapped to the nearest vertex of the owner part

unjoin.description: Charts to put back at their own packed place and out of their group

unwrap_id.description: The unwrap_id get_texture_unwrap (or the last answer) gave: with it, chart and vertex numbers are refused if the paint, the mesh or the seams changed since. Without it they are taken as they are

uv_edits.description: Move unwrapped vertices; the edit rides with its island

uv.description: Its place in the unwrap's mm, before the island's placement

vertex.description: An unwrapped vertex, as get_texture_unwrap lists with include_vertices

server_tools.description: Slice every plate in the project, the way the GUI's Slice All button does: one plate at a time until all are sliced. Pass all_plates=false to slice only the plate that is currently selected. status says what happened: slicing_started, or not_started with a reason and a message: busy_slicing (the pipeline is busy -- get_slicing_status's busy: a slice or Slice All run, an export, an upload, or the last slice still stopping; nothing is started -- call wait_for_slice, then slice_all again), already_sliced (nothing to do), busy_job (an arrange, an orient or a bed fill holds the app: poll get_slicing_status until ui_job is null, then slice_all again), invalid (the app refuses the plate as it stands -- its validation, an object partly off the plate, a filament check, missing plugins, a broken mixed filament, or a last slice that failed; message says which, in the app's words for a validation failure), nothing_to_slice (no printable object fully on the plates -- one partly off its plate or too tall for the printer does not count -- and no refusal the app gives words for), no_printer (the selected printer is the app's built-in default: none installed yet on a new data folder, or none selected; message and next_steps say how to install and select one) or unknown. Then call wait_for_slice, which returns once the run is over, with each plate's result; next_steps names the tool to call next. The plate selection walks from the first plate to the last while the run is in progress, and get_slicing_status puts back the plate that was selected here once it ends.

server_tools.name: slice_all

server_tools.description: Split an object as the object list's Split does. to: "objects" makes one object per solid part of a multi-part object, or per shell of a one-part object; its modifiers, negative volumes and support volumes are not carried (dropped_volumes lists them), and each piece keeps its place. When a piece would float and the object drops to the bed, keep_height (default true) keeps each piece at its height, false drops them onto the bed. The pieces are the last objects afterwards and every object after the split one moves down by one. to: "parts" splits one volume into one part per shell (name it with volume_id in a multi-part object); the pieces are named <name>_1, _2, ..., keep its filament, and stay in place. Painting is cleared unless keep_painting keeps it. One undo step. An open toolbar tool is closed first (closed_toolbar_tool). Refused while an arrange, orient or bed fill runs.

keep_height.description: to objects: keep a floating piece at its height (default true) or drop it onto the bed (false), the app's own question about floating pieces

keep_painting.description: Remap the painting (colour, supports, seams, fuzzy skin) onto the new meshes instead of clearing it; the app calls this experimental. Left out: the app's "Keep painted feature after mesh change" setting, which the answer's keep_painting_from names

to.description: objects: one object per solid part, or per shell of a one-part object; parts: one part per shell of a volume

server_tools.description: Batch transform multiple objects. Position, rotation and scale are all in the plate's own frame -- the same frame get_object_info reports -- not the object's local axes, and match move_object, rotate_object and scale_object exactly: a rotation or scale drops a resting object back onto the bed (Z=0), unless the entry gives position.z, which is kept as given. Each result carries rotate_object's placement fields for that object afterwards. Every entry is checked before any is applied: if one is rejected (an invalid object_id, a value that is not a number, or not an object where one is expected, a scale factor that is not positive), nothing is applied and results lists the rejected entries by their position (entry). One undo step undoes the whole batch.

rotation.description: Rotation about the plate's axes in degrees {x, y, z} - applied incrementally, X then Y then Z, about the object's centre

scale.description: Scale factors along the plate's axes {x, y, z}, or {uniform: value}; all must be positive
